checks.claim: Ropey 1.6.1 package and immutable commit identity
checks.conclusion: Package source VCS metadata and Cargo package version independently agree; manifests alone were not accepted as behavior evidence.

checks.claim: Shared Arc tree, cheap clones and qualified complexity
checks.conclusion: General complexity statement is attributed to upstream documentation. Arbitrary insertion is O(M + log N), not O(log N) independent of inserted text; final does not state that stronger bound.

checks.claim: Streaming UTF-8 construction through governing builder
checks.conclusion: Reader validates UTF-8, retains valid raw text, and constructs through RopeBuilder. Streaming construction is not a bounded-file-preview contract.

checks.claim: Chunked output can fail after partial emission
checks.conclusion: write_to calls write_all on chunk bytes and returns writer errors; it is not an atomic file-save protocol.

checks.claim: CRLF seam helper and governing callers are lower-level than F-082
checks.conclusion: Safe chunk seams prevent split scalars/CRLF; slicing may still split CRLF. No nearest-newline insertion or persistence policy follows.

checks.claim: Default CR feature, scalar indexing and byte/UTF-16 adapters
checks.conclusion: unicode_lines implies cr_lines; build features select line-count implementation. Public edits use scalar indices. UTF-16 interior indices round down to the containing scalar, so round trips require valid boundary preconditions.

checks.claim: Ropey 1.5.1 CRLF slice-count history
checks.conclusion: Changelog supports the historical fix description. Neither candidate nor reviewer establishes exact issue/fix-test ancestry. Final correctly does not offer it as a complete history witness.

checks.claim: Zed issue, merged fix and governing dirty/file context
checks.conclusion: Actual undo calls did_edit; dirty-to-clean, an extant File, Present DiskState and differing cached last-known mtime are required. This is not fresh filesystem IO or a universal conflict detector.

checks.claim: Named regression covers external write while dirty followed by undo
checks.conclusion: FakeFs integration test asserts stale dirty content before undo and external content/clean state afterward. Test source was inspected, not executed. It does not validate real NFS, filesystem races, Slint or Puppet Master.

checks.claim: Fix present in released v0.229.0 and upstream 28-check attribution
checks.conclusion: Release HTML resolves commit 7c07887d9555953bca7fe78417602114092ef8c8. Tag and commit-addressed code bytes agree. Presence in this release is established, not first affected/fixed release. Release notes do not themselves list #51037; final uses released source instead of the draft redirect claim. 28 checks is upstream PR page evidence only.

checks.claim: notify event-loss conditions and polling alternatives
checks.conclusion: Versioned docs support NFS no-events, large-watch-set loss, editor replacement event differences, PollWatcher and compare_contents options. No current defect inferred from an old issue.

checks.claim: TempPath persist atomic replacement differs from durability
checks.conclusion: Versioned API documents replacement, cross-filesystem limit and absence of file/directory synchronization. Final leaves protocol and platform selection open. API security conditions remain in captured bytes; no deployed implementation claimed.

checks.claim: Rust permissions, rename and direct-write failure conditions
checks.conclusion: Observed live docs identify std 1.99.0 (b940084d7, 2026-09-28). Metadata cannot predict effective write permission, rename differs by platform/mount, create truncates. Does not authorize bypassing product read-only Save block.

checks.claim: VS Code working-copy and backup lifecycle analogy
checks.conclusion: Mutable official wiki distinguishes resource/type and central lifecycle, restores backup as dirty and removes backups after clean save. Final only uses analogy, not exact native product or API equivalence.

checks.claim: Slint TextEdit long-text focus issue as conditional lead
checks.conclusion: Reporter gives Windows/1.10 and a TextEdit with wrap and key callback. No app version/control or current released defect is established. Final correctly retains unknown applicability.

checks.claim: Bounded unranked alternative representation tradeoffs
checks.conclusion: Upstream crop README, std String byte-index/insertion docs and Emacs gap description support stated general tradeoffs. Piece-table/mapped options are expressly uninspected categories, not recommendations or benchmarks.

checks.claim: Outside-update-to-undo edge is a useful proposal, not a current PM defect
checks.conclusion: Existing Save/focus prompt retained; no implication that every transition was already covered, no automatic reload imported.

checks.claim: Valid remaining owner questions and limited mechanism fit
checks.conclusion: Alias identity, platform save guarantees, recovery persistence, encoding/BOM, index units, distance/ties/no-surviving-boundary, decimal MB/MiB and stricter preview byte budget remain legitimate bounded unknowns. This does not excuse the already-fixed survivor, paste-off and cap-scope conditions in D01-D03.

checks.claim: Criticism corrections and useful options visibly survive
checks.conclusion: All admitted criticism families assessed. Corrected Ropey locator/default features, released-source locator, limited history, options and uncertainty survive. Contract-compression defects are separately counted, not excused by the critic accepting them.

checks.claim: Validation proposals are separated from actual execution
checks.conclusion: Eight later-validation groups; no PM build/test/benchmark/application witness is claimed. Source inspection and identities do not establish runtime acceptance. Host execution identity is not part of source judgment.

checks.claim: False unresolved disposition of nearest surviving newline after replacement
checks.conclusion: When a replacement removes the nearest original separator but another separator survives, the frozen acceptance criterion already limits inheritance to surviving boundaries. Final drops that selection condition and treats removed-neighbor behavior as unselected. Genuine ties/distance/no-survivor questions remain open, but removed separators are not eligible.

checks.claim: Paste-normalization-off byte preservation lost under unconditional new-boundary rule
checks.conclusion: For CRLF pasted next to LF with normalization off, frozen F-082 explicitly preserves pasted CRLF. Final says a newly inserted boundary inherits nearest, without the paste-off exception; limiting normalization to inserted text and testing on/off locality does not require off to preserve pasted endings. This is an authored-policy ambiguity/loss, not an observed PM data corruption claim.

checks.claim: Hard-cap scope weakened from every single buffer to editable full buffers
checks.conclusion: With the active cap at 5 MB, a larger full read-only buffer also violates the frozen never-load-more-than rule. Final protects editable full loading and makes preview byte budget open without retaining that absolute upper bound. Numeric values/visible alternatives are retained, but that narrower formulation is not unchanged cap scope.
